:::{#exm-integral-nonneg}
#### Integrals with respect to counting measure

Let $\mu$ be the counting measure on the die rolls $D$,
and let $g : D \to [0, \infty)$.
Every function on $D$ is measurable (@exm-measurable-function).

*The integral is the sum of the values.*
For any split of $D$ into nonempty pairwise disjoint sets $\dsn{A}$:

$$
\ba
\sumin \paren{\inf_{x \in A_i} g(x)} \mu(A_i)
&= \sumin \sum_{x \in A_i} \inf_{y \in A_i} g(y)
&& \text{(} \mu(A_i) \text{ counts the elements of } A_i \text{)} \\
&\le \sumin \sum_{x \in A_i} g(x)
&& \text{(an infimum is at most each value)} \\
&= \sum_{x \in D} g(x)
&& \text{(each } x \in D \text{ is in exactly one } A_i \text{)}
\ea
$$

The split into the six single points $\set{1}, \ldots, \set{6}$
gives exactly $\sum_{x \in D} g(x)$,
so the supremum is $\int_D g \, d\mu = \sum_{x \in D} g(x)$.
For example, with $g(x) = x$, $\int_D g \, d\mu = 1 + 2 + \cdots + 6 = 21$.

*An infinite integral.*
For the counting measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{N}$ and the constant function $h(n) = 1$,
the split with one set, $A_1 = \mathbb{N}$, gives the sum
$1 \cdot \mu(\mathbb{N}) = 1 \cdot \infty = \infty$,
so $\int_{\mathbb{N}} h \, d\mu = \infty$.

:::
